title: Power you switch on
sub: The fourth film of Locks before the data, the first series of Data protection and privacy: why robbers of the 1870s took bankers from their homes at night, and how a lock with a clock in it made the right numbers useless before their hour; the great power a data platform holds, in the storage, the admin settings and a table's history; a second account for each data specialist, its power off until it's switched on for a task, with a reason, a time, someone else's yes, an alert and a record; where a second account isn't practical, the power kept in the everyday account, switched off until a task needs it; and who never gets one.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's look, Night glass: a dark hall of frosted panes, frosted where what's behind may not be read and clear where it may. Cyan is an identity, green allowed, coral denied or closed, amber power switched on, violet hidden personal data. A passkey is a sealed card with a gold chip, never written out. The 1870s are painted in the same night light, with their place and year on a tag.
